daily_reality.summary: ADR professionals facilitate dispute resolution outside of court. Arbitrators conduct hearings and issue binding decisions; mediators help parties reach voluntary agreements; conciliators meet parties separately and make recommendations. Most work full time in private offices or meeting rooms.
typical_tasks: Conducting initial meetings with disputants to outline procedures, settle fees, and determine logistics
Reviewing claims, applications, contracts, and supporting documents
Researching applicable laws, regulations, policies, and precedent decisions
Scheduling and facilitating mediation or arbitration hearings
Interviewing claimants, agents, and witnesses to gather information
Managing hearing procedures: evidence submission, witness testimony, opening/closing statements
Drafting settlement agreements and arbitration awards
Managing virtual and hybrid hearing platforms
Conducting post-hearing analysis and writing reasoned decisions

deadlines.arbitration_award: Typically 30-60 days after hearing closes (varies by forum rules)
deadlines.aaa_consumer_response: 30 days for respondent to submit answering statement

daily_reality.seasonality: No strong seasonality. Case filings tend to increase at year-end and Q1 as businesses close books. Employment disputes may spike after annual performance review cycles.

regulatory.summary: Regulated at both federal and state levels. Federal Arbitration Act (FAA) governs enforcement. AAA and JAMS updated rules in 2025 to default to virtual hearings and expand employment/workplace coverage. State-level mediator certification varies: typically 20-40 hours training required.

key_laws.name: Federal Arbitration Act (FAA) — 9 U.S.C. §§ 1-16
key_laws.description: Federal law governing enforceability of arbitration agreements and awards

key_laws.name: Uniform Mediation Act (UMA)
key_laws.description: Model state law providing mediation confidentiality protections, adopted by ~12 states

key_laws.name: AAA Consumer & Employment Arbitration Rules (May 2025 update)
key_laws.description: Major rule updates: default virtual hearings, expanded workplace coverage, arbitrator subpoena authority

requirements: Bachelor's degree minimum; JD strongly preferred for arbitration
State-level mediator certification: typically 20-40 hours of mediation training
Some states require additional specialty training hours
AAA panelists: typically 10-15 years legal practice, 30-50% practice focus in relevant area
Continuing education: typically 4+ hours/year of mediation CE
No single national licensing body — varies by state and forum

regulatory.recent_changes: May 2025: AAA updated Consumer and Employment/Workplace rules — virtual hearings now default, arbitrators can issue subpoenas and order depositions, Employment rules renamed to cover independent contractor disputes. AAA launched AI arbitrator pilot for two-party documents-only construction cases.

Document management across multiple case platforms
No standardized cross-platform case management system
Virtual hearing fatigue and screen-time burden
Cybersecurity concerns with confidential case materials

terminology.summary: ADR has specialized vocabulary blending legal terminology with process-specific terms. Three main tracks (arbitration, mediation, conciliation) each have distinct procedural language.

terms.ADR: Alternative Dispute Resolution — umbrella term for non-litigation dispute resolution methods
terms.neutral: Third-party arbitrator, mediator, or conciliator acting impartially
terms.claimant: Party initiating the arbitration or mediation
terms.respondent: Party against whom a claim is filed
terms.demand for arbitration: Formal filing that initiates an arbitration case
terms.award: Arbitrator's binding decision resolving the dispute
terms.med-arb: Hybrid process: mediation first, then arbitration if mediation fails
terms.arb-med: Arbitration hearing first, award sealed; then mediation attempt; award opened only if mediation fails
terms.baseball arbitration: Each party submits a final offer; arbitrator must choose one (no splitting)
terms.high-low arbitration: Parties agree on a binding range; arbitrator's award falls within it
terms.caucus: Private meeting between mediator and one party during mediation
terms.impasse: Point where mediation negotiations reach a deadlock
terms.BATNA: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — party's fallback option
terms.WATNA: Worst Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement
terms.discovery: Pre-hearing exchange of information and documents
terms.interim measures: Temporary relief ordered by an arbitrator before final award
terms.manifest disregard: Legal standard for challenging arbitration awards (extremely limited)
terms.panel: Group of arbitrators (typically 3) hearing a case together
terms.submission agreement: Agreement to submit an existing dispute to arbitration

career_psychology.summary: Second-career profession for many — most enter after 10-20+ years in law, retired judges, or subject matter experts. Moderate median salary ($67,710 BLS) but top arbitrators at JAMS/AAA earn $300-1,000+/hour. Intellectual satisfaction is high; workload control is a key motivator.
career_path: Law degree (JD) or advanced degree in relevant field
10-20+ years of legal practice or subject matter expertise
Mediation training (40+ hours) and state certification
Court-annexed mediation roster (volunteer or low-fee cases for experience)
ADR provider panel application (AAA, JAMS, NAM)
Senior panelist at major ADR provider / retired judge neutral
fears: Insufficient caseload to sustain independent practice
Being removed from provider panels for low ratings
Issuing a challenged or vacated award damaging reputation
Difficulty building initial reputation without established network
motivation: Continued engagement after retirement from bench/practice
High hourly rates at senior levels
burnout_factors: Emotional weight of contentious disputes (family, employment)
Administrative burden of managing independent practice
Isolation of independent practice without firm support

community.summary: Professional community organized through major ADR providers (AAA, JAMS), the ABA Dispute Resolution Section, and specialized associations. Growing online presence and CLE/conference ecosystem.

events: ABA Section of Dispute Resolution Annual Spring Conference

market.summary: Stable growth market. BLS projects 4% growth 2024-2034 (~9,500 total positions). ADR expanding into gig economy, tech, and healthcare disputes. AAA piloting AI arbitration. Virtual hearings now standard. Top neutrals earn very high fees; entry-level market more competitive.
market_trends: Virtual hearings now default under AAA 2025 rules — expanding geographic reach
AAA piloting AI arbitrator for small construction disputes
Employment/Workplace rules expanded to cover independent contractors and gig workers
Mass arbitration claims from consumer tech creating new demand
Healthcare and technology sectors increasingly using in-house arbitrators
Growing demand for international arbitration specialists
Some legislative efforts to restrict mandatory arbitration clauses
